task: Core #1186 F6-U03a: reviewed source/connection guard only; no DB writes

assuranceCeiling.rationale: The F6-U03 work is the prerequisite to a potentially destructive disposable database reprovision, so source-byte authority, connection identity, negative tests and exact-head review must be proven before introducing any runnable reset. This first narrow unit creates only a non-executing diagnostic and its negative tests; it explicitly does not authorize SQL DDL, cloud workflow activation, or the 59-file hosted replay.

acceptanceCriteria: The reviewer can call the source verifier against the canonical Git repository and observe a fixed reviewed SHA plus exactly 59 migration-file identities and the required five baseline companions.
A regression fixture with unchanged SQL names but modified bytes must be rejected, including mutation of corrected 0058 and all middle customer migrations.
All unauthorized libpq environment selectors, invalid Supabase project hosts, databases or usernames, and absent trusted TLS material must fail before any child process could start.
The published module exports only review and inert planning functions; its execution mode remains disabled and no real database client or schema write is introduced.
Full canonical CI verification and evidence must be tied to exact head, not an inherited earlier Core release claim.
invariants: Only the preapproved disposable Fresh Install reference istjjkdcvsvilrycqecd is ever accepted as a syntactic database target.
The 59 customer-baseline files and five required companions must match the exact reviewed F6-U02 source commit byte-for-byte before source verification may pass.
Unknown, extra, duplicate or altered migration files cause source verification to BLOCK rather than create a new baseline checksum on demand.
No operation in F6-U03a may send SQL, drop a schema, delete Storage content or alter any Supabase project.
Original Alap customer Office communication and Pro team chat rules remain unchanged and are not claimed to be behaviorally verified.
forbiddenStates: A script that runs destructive SQL or connects to a real Supabase instance during unit tests.
An inherited PGHOSTADDR or PGSERVICE changing libpq routing behind the reviewed target URL.
Previously unreviewed SQL bytes being treated as approved solely because their filenames or count match.
An explicit execution authorization being interpreted as permission to wipe the hosted disposable project.
Source-only checks being reported as successful hosted Fresh Install or Alap-Pro tenant RLS proof.

failureModes: Changed intermediate SQL bytes but identical filenames or file count pass an insufficient verifier.
Local environment PGHOSTADDR or PGSERVICE overrides an otherwise correctly checked database URL.
Unknown or modified psql meta-command is evaluated by a later shell despite a trusted SQL file name.
TLS downgrade or untrusted certificate allows a wrong endpoint during a future live connection.
An executable reset is accidentally enabled by an ordinary branch build or a generic continue request.
A future audit conflates this static source verification with hosted schema or signed-in RLS readiness.
edgeCases: Historical baseline includes two valid, differently named 0026 migration files that must both remain in the ordered list.
Postgres URL includes %-encoded malformed characters, extra sslmode parameters, or an alternate database name.
The reviewed ancestor commit does not exist in a shallow clone, is not an ancestor, or resolves to a rewritten branch.
An attacker adds a SQL file outside the expected customer-baseline folder, edits auth bootstrap or changes neutral seed.
A caller supplies inherited PGSSLROOTCERT, PGOPTIONS, PGHOSTADDR or case-sensitive libpq environment selectors.
A source file contains a psql include or shell meta-command that must never be trusted for a later replay.

alternatives.summary: Use the existing canonical source and Git-reviewed blob identities in an inert verifier with explicit libpq/TLS guards and negative tests.
alternatives.reason: Maintains one authority, permits reproducible fail-closed tests and prevents creating a second deploy engine or activating data deletion in the preparatory release unit.

alternatives.summary: Directly clear the current disposable project and apply the migrations using a combined ad hoc SQL command.
alternatives.reason: Skips repo Plan Before Code, exact reviewed source confirmation and atomic failure injection and can destroy the only known previous proof schema.

alternatives.summary: Introduce an independent migration management service that controls all resets and keeps its own schema inventory.
alternatives.reason: Would duplicate existing Fresh Install, Development Guard and Completion Truth authorities, expanding permissions and future maintenance without resolving the specific defect.

specialistReviews.finding: The candidate must reject PGHOSTADDR and other inherited libpq selectors; a validated URI alone does not identify the actual remote endpoint.
specialistReviews.resolution: Use fail-closed selector validation and minimum TLS verified configuration; defer network validation and DDL to a separately approved later unit.

specialistReviews.finding: Exact migration filenames are insufficient because mutable bodies can conceal different DDL and breach reproducible source evidence.
specialistReviews.resolution: Pin every baseline artifact to immutable reviewed commit object identities; reject changed bodies and all unauthorized extra SQL files.

specialistReviews.finding: The current preflight fails on an occupied disposable schema and previous Office tests never established safe live replay behavior.
specialistReviews.resolution: Do not add any runner to the hosted Fresh Install workflow in F6-U03a; keep live transaction/rollback as a future gated work unit.

specialistReviews.finding: A new module must inherit known failures in quality-infrastructure and avoid reporting source similarity as completed runtime evidence.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep accepted source-readiness distinct from hosted proof and bind the test suite to exact-head existing CI and Completion Truth gates.

challenge.scenario: A forged SQL migration keeps its existing number and basename but substitutes executable SQL body.
challenge.finding: The old prototype checked paths and count without cryptographically binding each body to a reviewed Git commit.
challenge.resolution: Compare every local byte to its exact approved Git blob object and reject any mismatched body before returning REVIEW.

challenge.scenario: The repository contains all 59 expected SQL files but one required Auth bootstrap file is modified.
challenge.finding: Source integrity of migrations alone does not establish the complete bootstrap and postflight evidence contract.
challenge.resolution: Pin the manifest, Auth bootstrap, seed and pre/postflight files to the same immutable reviewed Git ancestor.

challenge.scenario: A user sets PGHOSTADDR to an unrelated IP while providing an approved-looking Postgres database URL.
challenge.finding: libpq may select destinations from inherited process variables that contradict lexical URL verification.
challenge.resolution: Reject conflicting PG environment selectors and construct a strict minimal child configuration with verified host and TLS authority.

challenge.scenario: The supplied database URL contains a staging project reference with a valid looking password.
challenge.finding: Checking for the substring Fresh Install or database name alone cannot distinguish neighboring Supabase projects.
challenge.resolution: Accept only exact approved hostname and project-scoped database username combinations, rejecting unrecognized hosts and usernames.

challenge.scenario: The server certificate is absent or the caller requests permissive sslmode during a future database connection.
challenge.finding: A valid-looking Supabase project URL is not proof that a network peer authenticates as the expected host.
challenge.resolution: Require verify-full TLS and explicit trusted CA file, and keep actual connection checks outside this inert preparatory unit.

challenge.scenario: A newer unreviewed migration file is appended beside 0058 without updating the prior source pin.
challenge.finding: An implementation that checks only the first and last filename can replay an unauthorized addition.
challenge.resolution: Require the full expected reviewed Git file set and reject extra or missing SQL files regardless of their apparent ordering.

challenge.scenario: The future replay is triggered automatically by pushing an otherwise harmless branch to GitHub.
challenge.finding: The setup has not yet proven safe DB-side rollback or the consequence of unexpected connection loss.
challenge.resolution: Keep execution hard-disabled and omit all database-executing code paths and cloud secrets from F6-U03a.

challenge.scenario: A tester treats the source verification report as proof that signed-in Alap and Pro Office permissions are correct.
challenge.finding: Static Git contents cannot establish actual deployed RLS policy results for customer and internal chat tenants.
challenge.resolution: Bound this unit to source and connection guard readiness only; future live actor-and-tenant proofs remain blocking.

challenge.scenario: The working branch is based on a closed F6-U02 development transaction whose plan appears already verified.
challenge.finding: The inherited plan has an obsolete base SHA and does not authorize unrelated new scripts or security-sensitive behavior.
challenge.resolution: Use a fresh Development Guard generated plan and new changeBaseSha from the exact F6-U03 preimplementation commit.

proofPlan: Run the canonical F6-U03 Development Guard on a full GitHub checkout and require exact base SHA, active failure coverage and reviewed scoped work list.
Verify Plan Before Code with nine adversarial scenarios and role-scoped negative tests before introducing a new source-verification implementation file.
Run focused Node test suite with deliberately modified intermediate SQL, altered bootstrap, added migration, forged Git commit and unsafe psql include fixtures.
Run explicit TLS/connection negative tests for project, database, username and inherited libpq environment conflicts without spawning real Postgres.
Run exact-branch edit-time guard, incremental replay, knowledge preflight and CI quality, typecheck and truth reporting for the final head.
Confirm the Fresh Install database remains unmodified and that no DDL runner or cloud secret is used during this first quality-infrastructure release unit.
operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: The current sandbox-only candidate has previously accepted modified SQL source bytes and inherited libpq redirecting environment variables. An accidentally promoted executable reset could therefore replay unreviewed migrations or contact the wrong Postgres service. F6-U03a must close both classes of defect before any downstream database action can be proposed.
observableOutcomes: An exact Git-reviewed F6-U02 source ancestor and the complete 59-file ordered baseline, manifest, bootstrap, neutral seed and pre/postflight are required before source verification returns a reviewed result.
Deliberately modified SQL with unchanged filenames, unknown added or removed files, forged manifests and unreviewed psql meta-commands produce deterministic blocked outcomes in regression tests.
Connection validation rejects platform/staging/wrong database, inherited libpq redirection variables, missing CA or downgraded TLS; no PostgreSQL subprocess is spawned by this unit.
Canonical Development Guard, Plan Before Code and TypeScript/quality checks must pass on the exact modified repository branch before code is eligible for integration.
unresolvedRisks: Offline source and connection checks alone do not prove real Postgres project identity against a live TLS connection, transaction rollback or the historical schema provenance.
The next release unit must independently validate actual reversible hosted reprovision, Storage-managed state, 59 real migrations and actor/tenant Alap-Pro RLS behavior.

in: Author one explicitly non-executable, shared quality-infrastructure source and connection identity verification module based on the offline prototype.
Add Node/TypeScript negative regression coverage for exact pinned source and libpq/TLS guards; preserve existing Fresh Install authority.
Keep the existing F6-U03 plan documentation aligned with security findings and evidence claims.
out: No Supabase database write, schema drop, migration, secret manipulation, storage deletion or realtime project state change.
No changes to the main Fresh Install deploy workflow, platform or staging project and no permission to execute a destructive runner.
No Builder, Factory, template development or unrelated Core transaction changes.
